rows.answer: The build fails at link time because the `sandbox::checksum` function is declared in `include/sandbox/ring_buffer.hpp` but not implemented. The function needs to be defined in `src/ring_buffer.cpp` to resolve the undefined reference error.

The ring_buffer test is failing due to a logic error in the `full()` method implementation. The bug is in src/ring_buffer.cpp line 29 where the condition `count_ + 1 == slots_.size()` should be `count_ == slots_.size()`. This causes the ring buffer to incorrectly report itself as full when it still has one slot available, preventing valid push operations from succeeding.

history.name: propose_patch

arguments.find: bool RingBuffer::full() const { return count_ + 1 == slots_.size(); }
arguments.replace: bool RingBuffer::full() const { return count_ == slots_.size(); }
arguments.rationale: The bug is in the full() method logic. It should return true when the count equals the capacity, not when count + 1 equals the capacity. With a capacity of 3, the buffer should be considered full when it has 3 elements, not when it has 2 elements. This was causing the push(3) operation to fail incorrectly on the third push.

rows.answer: Fixed the ring_buffer test failure by correcting the logic in the full() method. The bug was that the method returned true when count_ + 1 == slots_.size() instead of count_ == slots_.size(), causing incorrect full state reporting. After applying the fix, all tests now pass.

The test "text_util" is crashing due to a segmentation fault caused by a deliberate null pointer dereference in the trim function in src/text_util.cpp at line 38. When the input string contains only whitespace characters, the code attempts to dereference a null pointer, which causes the crash. The test calls sandbox::trim("   ") which triggers this issue.

The test named "slow" does not terminate due to an infinite loop in tests/test_slow.cpp. The loop uses an unsigned char variable 'i' that wraps around to 0 after reaching 255, causing the condition i < 300 to always be true. This results in an infinite loop that causes the test to timeout.

The RingBuffer class is defined in include/sandbox/ring_buffer.hpp and implemented in src/ring_buffer.cpp. When pushing to a full buffer, the push method returns false without overwriting existing data, as confirmed by the implementation in src/ring_buffer.cpp lines 7-15.
